narrative:
Shipping velocity: one request has shipped and one is nearly done, all on 2026-11-03. The unit option went from ask (12:22) to commit (12:23) in under a minute of recorded time, and the significantDigits option reached a passing suite within about 30 seconds of its ask, with no commit recorded yet.

## Forced unit option for prettyBytes (2026-11-03)

The owner asked for a `unit` option on prettyBytes that forces the output unit. Their examples were `{unit: 'MB'}`, which gives `0.00134 MB`, and `{unit: 'B'}`, which gives `1337 B`. The unit has to belong to the system chosen by the `bits` and `binary` options. A unit outside that system should throw a TypeError, the same as the other option checks. The owner also asked for readme, types and tests in the same change.

The agent inspected UNIT_SETS in index.js, implemented the option, and added the readme section, runtime tests and a type assertion. The suite passed and the owner approved with "Good, commit it". The work was committed as b7f87a0 at 12:23.

After the release, a stale saved preference (`unit: 'KB'`) crashed the owner's storage dashboard file table. The owner changed policy: new options must ignore bad values and format as if unset, while `unit` keeps its throw until the next major release. A follow-up added a `{bits: true, unit: 'Mbit'}` readme example and test, committed as e2991bc. Memory records no PR or version number. The throwing behavior remains an unfixed regression, left in place on purpose.

## Significant digits option (2026-11-03)

At 12:30 the owner asked for a `significantDigits` option that changes the default 3-digit rounding. For 1337 it gives `1.3 kB` at 2 digits and `1.337 kB` at 4. It applies only when the fraction-digit options are unset. They asked for "Readme, types and tests as usual."

The agent mapped the toPrecision logic in index.js, which uses a minimum of 3 digits. It then added the option to the implementation, types and readme. Following the new policy, invalid values fall back to 3 digits instead of throwing. Tests cover 1 to 4 digits, integer-part preservation, fraction-option precedence and the invalid fallback, plus a type assertion. npm test passes with 55 tests. The request is at about 80%, with no commit, PR or release recorded.

## What this teaches so far

The owner writes concrete requests: they give example outputs, name the failure behavior, and list the supporting deliverables up front. Agents should treat validation, documentation, type definitions and tests as part of the feature itself.

A shipped throw caused a production crash, and the owner turned that into a standing rule within minutes. The next option applied it straight away. Agents should default to forgiving handling of bad input for new options, and should not change shipped behavior before a major release.
